slot.brief: Circuit diagram: Zener regulator with a series resistor, source voltage and load; compute current through the Zener diode at stated input voltage using the load voltage remaining fixed.

stem: In the circuit shown, an ideal Zener diode maintains the load voltage at its breakdown voltage. Find the current through the Zener diode when the input is $12$ V.

verdicts.working: At 6 V, the 200 Ω resistor supplies (12−6)/200 = 30 mA. The 300 Ω load draws 6/300 = 20 mA, so the Zener current is 10 mA.

working:
$V_{\text{out}}=6\ \text{V}$
$I_s=\dfrac{12-6}{200}=30\ \text{mA}$; $I_L=\dfrac{6}{300}=20\ \text{mA}$
$I_Z=I_s-I_L=10\ \text{mA}$ Independent check: At 6 V, the 200 Ω resistor supplies (12−6)/200 = 30 mA. The 300 Ω load draws 6/300 = 20 mA, so the Zener current is 10 mA.
solution:
The Zener clamps the load voltage at $6\ \text{V}$. The series current is $I_s=\dfrac{12-6}{200}=30\ \text{mA}$, while the load current is $I_L=\dfrac{6}{300}=20\ \text{mA}$.
$$I_Z=I_s-I_L=30-20=10\ \text{mA}$$

figure.description: Draw a 12 V DC source with its positive terminal connected through a 200 ohm series resistor to an output node; the negative terminal is the common return. Connect a 6 V Zener diode in reverse bias between the output node and return, with its cathode at the output node. Connect a 300 ohm load resistor in parallel with the Zener between the same output node and return. Label the source 12 V, the series resistor 200 ohm, the Zener 6 V, and the load 300 ohm.

draft.distractor_notes: A: incorrect current subtraction; C: reports the load current; D: reports the series current without subtracting load current.
